body:
The owner asked agents to start merging this repository into `Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo`. Until all work moves there, the two repositories are mirrored, and no history is lost. This PR turns that into standing work in the prompt and the action list.

## What changes
- **`prompt.md`**: "End state: one repository" (which said "the owner decides when the move resumes") becomes **Repository merge: mirror, then move**:
  - One writer at a time. This repository's `main` is the source until cutover, and `oss-monorepo/research/` is a copy that a sync refreshes. Nobody edits the copy directly.
  - No history loss. Every commit reaches oss-monorepo with its original hash. Squash, rebase, cherry-pick, hand-copy, force-push and in-place `filter-repo` are all ruled out, and a mirror PR merges only with a merge commit.
  - The tree stays movable.
  - Cutover belongs to the owner: make oss-monorepo public, repoint the scheduled runs, then archive this repository (never delete it).
  - The mirror milestones come before picking a track. `runs.jsonl` gains a `mirror` task type.
- **`PROJECTS.md`**: a new **Repository merge (before the tracks)** section is the action list. It holds the fixed path map, the sync script, and seven milestones: `mirror-movable`, `mirror-tool`, `mirror-guards`, `mirror-import`, `mirror-retire-6143`, `mirror-sync` and `mirror-cutover`. Each milestone is claimed through its PR title, as tracks are. Milestones that push to oss-monorepo follow that repository's `CLAUDE.md`, except that they merge with a merge commit.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: replaces the "move is on hold" note. The file will also be read as `research/CLAUDE.md` inside the mirror, so it now tells readers there not to edit the copy.

## Why this mechanism rather than #6143's or `filter-repo`
- **`filter-repo` rewrites every hash.** The hashes in `prompts/runs.jsonl` and old links would then point at nothing.
- **#6143 used a one-off move commit.** Later syncs would depend on rename detection, so a new top-level file here (such as `PROJECTS.md`, added after 2026-10-01) would land at oss-monorepo's root.
- **The sync here avoids both.** Each sync is `git merge -s ours` with research `main` as the second parent, after which `research/` is replaced by the path map of that commit. Original hashes survive, every sync places files the same way, and projects keep their `research/<slug>/` paths, so `git log -- research/<slug>` works with no `--follow`.

## Verified (scratch clones, 2026-10-14)
- I ran the script exactly as written in `PROJECTS.md` on oss-monorepo `main` (`a05ae6b4`) against research `main` (`a820eac`):
  - The result is a two-parent merge, and only `research/` changed.
  - The trees of `research/site` and `research/selfrep-closure` equal the research commit's.
  - `git log -- research/<slug>` shows the original hashes, for example `255c3da` and `99736c5`.
- A second sync after one new research commit brought in exactly that commit plus the merge. A new top-level file landed at `research/<name>`.
- #6143 holds 14 commits found in neither `main`. All of them are that session's own: the move commit, merges, CI hardening, the Hetzner clean-up and the Pages wiring. Every research commit it carries is already an ancestor of this `main`, so retiring it loses nothing.
- `python site/build.py`: `ok: 392 projects, 3421 tests`.

A companion PR in oss-monorepo updates its `prompt.md` and `land-your-work.md` to match.
